release_line: v1.8.1 (2026-11-10); the trial ran the checkout at the pin, not a release
node: v24.22.2 (vendored under _vendor; nimo system node is v22, below the >=24 engine)

sandbox.how: unshare -rn (own user+network namespace, loopback only) + sandlock 0.8.9 --no-supervisor (Landlock fs: read system dirs, the checkout, node, lane scripts; write only the stage dir under ./tmp) + clean env + throwaway HOME; local model reached only through one unix socket forwarded to Ollama
sandbox.why_not_supervisor: sandlock supervisor mode answers readlink on a non-symlink with ENOENT instead of EINVAL, so glibc realpath (Node fs.realpath.native) fails and the hub cannot start; --no-supervisor cannot take --net-allow, hence the namespace

upstream_tests.cmd: node --test 'tests/!(simulation).test.ts' (npm test:quick) in the same sandbox

local_model.agent: use: command (one Ollama call per round)

lane.reply: A developer can use local-h to perform a quick smoke test on a catalog lane by running a simple command in their terminal.

paused_rule.note: an event that arrives while a rule is paused is logged and dropped, not queued

comparison.headless_runs: tie: both run CLI agents headless; Autoloop via a resident hub + worker, ours via systemd-run units from an hourly timer
comparison.park_and_resume: Autoloop better at the mechanics (zero-process wait, answer resumes the same lane with the answer in context, card CLI); ours re-opens parks by rule (main green, backoff, 2 retries) which Autoloop has no equivalent for
comparison.decision_cards_vs_hard_stops: ours better for this job: hard stops are machine-checked rules (data/promotion-rules.json); in Autoloop whether to ask is the agent's judgment from an askFirst list in a Chinese prompt
comparison.concurrency_caps: Autoloop: running cap only (group parallel, worker.capacity, maxActive), measured max 4; no daily cap, so 20 a day would need our counter
comparison.crash_recovery: Autoloop better: SQLite event log, card and running lane survived hub SIGKILL, lane ran once; ours: noclobber markers + lock, also idempotent
comparison.per_lane_isolation: ours better: one git worktree and branch per lane; Autoloop gives a rule-level cwd only, per-lane worktrees would still be our script
comparison.local_models: tie at the command level (Ollama lane ran); session resume needs a plugin per agent; no Grok Build plugin; opencode is ACP handshake-only upstream
comparison.setup_and_maintenance: ours cheaper to keep: Autoloop adds Node 24, a resident daemon with an HTTP port and SQLite, Chinese CLI and prompts, and a 1-week-old codebase shipping several releases a day
comparison.activity: very active but new: first commit 2026-11-03, 186 commits, 4.4k stars, 806 forks, v1.8.1 on 2026-11-10, ~75% of commits by one author
